## Results

- Search 4 (Precision Nutrition & Microbiome, n=464 papers): 3 of 8 research clusters flagged as under-reviewed at cosine < 0.30
- Five demo corpora built from PubMed (9,212 / 490 / 151 / 464 / 5,977 papers), each with review and non-review splits
- Methodology paper accepted with revisions

## The problem

Research teams deciding where a new systematic review is needed can't manually read thousands of abstracts to see which areas of primary research the existing reviews haven't covered.

## What I built

PubMed Entrez query split by publication type (review vs non-review) -> TF-IDF (1-2 grams) -> TruncatedSVD(100) -> k-means (also DBSCAN, agglomerative, LDA; Doc2Vec/FastText options) -> cluster-level TF-IDF cosine similarity between research and review clusters -> clusters with max similarity < 0.3 flagged as candidate gaps. Batch vignettes for 5 precision-nutrition searches.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What it is for

Supports a portfolio or prioritization decision (which topics merit a new evidence synthesis), analogous to horizon scanning of a research portfolio. Currently only valid as exploratory triage for human review.
:::

## Tools

Python, Streamlit, Biopython (Entrez), scikit-learn, gensim, umap-learn, Plotly
